soundness_flags.label: ass:density-envelope-compatible
soundness_flags.one_line: On the unit-volume cube, the density condition in ass:context-density already implies c_X≤∫p_X=1≤C_X, so this separate load-bearing assumption is redundant.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves a finite-arm regret–ATE point-estimation-error tradeoff and an EXP3E attainment result; Theorem 5 is a high-probability error bound for its nominated estimator.
The paper studies CATE estimation against welfare regret with matched multi-objective bounds and privacy-preserving designs.
The article studies inference for the mean outcome under an optimal individualized treatment strategy, gives a pathwise-differentiability characterization, and describes root-n confidence intervals.
The paper establishes asymptotically minimax estimation results for L_r norms in Gaussian white noise using nonsmooth-functional methods.
The paper uses adaptively reweighted augmented inverse-propensity scores to obtain asymptotically normal policy-evaluation statistics under adaptive experiments.
CADR is an asymptotically normal estimator for a contextual policy value under adaptive data collection.
Penalized EXP4 yields stability and Wald inference for fixed linear functionals, plus near-minimax regret up to logarithmic factors.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Delete ass:density-envelope-compatible and cite the unit-volume integration consequence directly in the two witness theorems.

Promote one explicit non-fixed-gap Hölder branch from the bump lemma into a provisional rate proposition, including its exact budget range and the corresponding lower-bound packing, before asking for the complete piecewise frontier.
State the fixed-design rho≈T reduction as an anchored comparison theorem against a specific positive-part-functional honest-inference rate, rather than only as a required sanity reduction.

recommended_next_step: Remove the redundant density-envelope assumption, then advance the otherwise novel and well-posed frontier program to Stage 0.
